thread:
maya: Hey, heads-up — our TypeScript sample app fails when run on Deno/Bun. Error looks like ESM/CJS mismatch.
kevin: Are you pulling the CJS bundle by accident? Deno/Bun need an ESM entrypoint.
maya: I just `import { Redwood } from 'redwood'` and Deno throws: `Uncaught SyntaxError: The requested module ".../redwood/dist/index.cjs" does not provide an export named 'Redwood'`.
olga: That usually means package.json exports map is routing to a CJS file. Can you paste the import snippet and the generated path?
maya: snippet: ```ts
// main.ts
import { Redwood } from "redwood"
const r = new Redwood({ apiKey: Deno.env.get('REDWOOD_KEY') })
await r.generate('hello')
```
samir: Also seeing runtime errors on Bun: `crypto.randomBytes is not a function`. SDK is using Node builtin crypto & Buffer in a few places (retry backoff id, HMAC signing). Edge runtimes expect `globalThis.crypto.subtle` + Uint8Array.
kevin: Two separate but related issues: 1) package exports/entrypoints (ESM vs CJS) 2) runtime assumptions (node globals). We should treat Deno/Bun/edge as first-class.
david: Agree. For auth + retry behavior: our retry logic uses `setTimeout` + `http.Agent` options in Node. On edge (Vercel Edge, Cloudflare Workers) there's no Agent and no process.env. That breaks header/timeout code paths.
maya: On Vercel Edge I get `ReferenceError: process is not defined` when trying to read env for API key in the example.
olga: Quick fixes: - add an ESM build at dist/esm/index.js - add package.json "exports" map with conditional exports for "import" and "require" - runtime feature detection for crypto/process.
samir: For cryptography: prefer webcrypto APIs if available, fallback to node crypto. Example detection: `const randomBytes = typeof globalThis.crypto?.getRandomValues === 'function' ? (n)=>{const a=new Uint8Array(n); globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues(a); return a} : require('crypto').randomBytes`
kevin: For types: Deno complains about typings that reference `Buffer` or Node builtin types. We should ship typings that use Uint8Array and conditional types, or separate `types-deno.d.ts`.
maya: For a short-term workaround I was able to import the raw ESM dist file: `import { Redwood } from 'redwood/dist/esm/index.js'` — works, but that's not great for DX.
david: We should also add small example apps under /examples/deno and /examples/bun to run in CI. Run `deno test` and `bun test` on those to catch regressions.
ci-bot: @maya opened issue #1423 (deno/bun support) and linked failing sample app + stack trace.
olga: Also: document recommended import lines in README with a compat matrix: Node (CJS/ESM), Edge (vercel/cloudflare), Deno, Bun. Spell out known limitations (streams, abort controller behavior, web-crypto differences).
samir: Another gotcha: Bun's fetch behaves like web fetch but its `FormData`/stream impl differs; our retry layer assumes `response.body.getReader()` exists. Need defensive checks.
kevin: Plan I'm going to PR: 1) publish dist/esm + update package.exports 2) runtime detection for crypto/Buffer/env 3) simplify retry to not depend on Node-only Agent 4) add deno/bun examples + CI 5) update types to avoid Buffer in public surface.
maya: Thanks — any timeline? this is blocking a partner demo tomorrow.
kevin: I'll try to get a minimal PR today that at least provides an ESM export and runtime crypto detection. If that lands we can unblock the demo.
david: I'll pair review once you open it. Also add a short note in changelog and examples.
maya: :thumbsup: much appreciated, will follow issue #1423 for updates.
kevin: FYI — I'll add small polyfill snippet to examples for people stuck on older runtimes:
```js
// polyfill-web-crypto.js (examples)
if (typeof globalThis.crypto === 'undefined') {
  const { randomBytes } = await import('crypto')
  globalThis.crypto = { getRandomValues: (arr) => { const b = randomBytes(arr.length); arr.set(b) } }
}
```
olga: Nice. Also add test that ensures `import 'redwood'` works in Node ESM and Deno with the exports map.
ci-bot: Created PR checklist item: run sample-app on Deno/Bun playgrounds.
maya: Cool — I'll try the `dist/esm` import if the PR lands. Thanks y'all!
